newsitem.title: USA: Family Golf execs address Q4 EPS shortfall.
newsitem.headline: Family Golf execs address Q4 EPS shortfall.

text.p: Executives at Family Golf Centers Inc said that accounting troubles, including higher-than-expected depreciation costs, nicked about $0.05 a share off fourth quarter profits.

Speaking on a conference call, Chairman and Chief Executive Dominic Chang said higher depreciation costs took about a half million dollars off fourth quarter net income. The company also said it was charged additional taxes on shares issued in July. The two combined to about $0.05 a share, he said.
Earlier, Family Golf posted earnings per share of $0.04 a share, missing analyst's estimates of $0.09 a share and sending the stock off over 20 percent in early trading.

Chang said the depreciation costs "were my fault. We didn't pay much attention to getting the appraisal reports in on time," which meant depreciation costs for several acquisitions could not be booked until the fourth quarter.
He said the company now plans to spend more to get appraisals in a more timely fashion although the higher costs are not expected to be material.
Chang said Family Golf plans to continue its aggressive growth plan. "That means the spike in depreciation in the fourth quarter will continue through 1997."

He estimated 1997 depreciation at $4.0 to $4.5 million because of the planned new facilities. Previously, it had estimated 1997 depreciation at $2.0 - $2.5 million. In 1996, depreciation was $2.1 million and in 1995, about $800,000.

Chang said Family Golf plans to end 1997 with roughly 65 centers by adding 27 new facilities, but said delays could easily keep the number slightly lower, to roughly 25. It plans about the same amount of acquisitions in 1998, he said.

Chief Financial Officer Krishnan Thampi said the company had about $40 million in cash on its balance sheet and $16 million in debt at year-end. He also agreed, in response to an analysts' question, that the higher depreciation costs could help the company's after-tax cash flow because of a tax shelter on the depreciation.
He said one of the reasons for the higher depreciation costs was that in several instances, the relative value of the land fell while the value of the building and improvements to the land did not.

Family Golf also said that based on some delays in receiving construction permits in 1996, it urged analysts to expect slightly longer time frame for a new center to go from acquisition to grand opening. Currently, analysts are estimating about three to four months, but the company urged a time frame of about six months.
It said gross margins in its pro-shops were slightly lower, citing the need to push brand name items which carry lower margins in new shops in order to establish credibility with new customers.

Chang said prices for acquisitions have not yet been affected by the emergence of rival companies, including Jack Niklaus' Golden Bear Golf Inc and MetroGolf Inc. "We have not had direct competition with (Golden Bear) except in one instance in Los Angeles," he said.
